fields.why: Tables 1-2 give weighted up-to-date percentages for 3+ levels of age (cervical), race, education, poverty, insurance, U.S. residence and sexual orientation, each with a Wald F P-value.
Each listed SPD has 3+ compared levels (insurance counted as SES); sex and Hispanic ethnicity are pairs, and usual source of care and year are not SPDs.

Wald F tests 'for any differences across ... groups' are omnibus tests over each SPD's levels. The flag is a false alarm: the side-by-side entry is the four Hispanic subgroups, whose P-value (table note) tests only Hispanic vs non-Hispanic, so no test spans the subgroups.

brief_issues: The mechanical check could exempt a side-by-side entry whose groups are subgroups under a test stated to cover only the parent pair (here Hispanic subgroups under a Hispanic vs non-Hispanic P-value).
